subprompt_extra:
Working agreements (TokenPal):
- Python 3.12+. `ruff check tokenpal/` (line-length 100, E/F/I/N/W/UP) and `mypy tokenpal/ --ignore-missing-imports` (strict) must both pass on your worktree before you commit.
- pytest with asyncio_mode=auto. Write the failing test first; prove it ran.
- Grep before adding a helper, constant, or field. If the pattern already exists in tokenpal/, reuse it.
- Don't abstract on the first use. No ABC, registry, or config dataclass until there is a second concrete consumer.
- Don't add state nothing reads. A field with no reader is speculative -- delete it.
- No narrative comments. Comments earn space only for hidden constraints, surprising invariants, or a workaround for a specific bug.
- Privacy contract: desktop-content tools are marked `reads_desktop_content` and must never reach memory.db or any log line. Do not add a marked tool to M3_CATALOG or M1_RULES. See docs/claude/actions.md.
- Path safety lives in tokenpal/util/paths.py (`resolve_inside`, `path_is_sensitive`, `REJECT_PATH`, `git_root`). Reuse it rather than hand-rolling containment.
- Commit message must contain `Fixes #N` (not just `(#N)`) or GitHub will not auto-close the issue.
- Use the commit trailers the dispatching session gives you in this prompt. Do not copy a session URL out of this config file -- it has none on purpose.
- Do not touch plans/, CLAUDE.md, or .parallel-issues.json unless your issue names them.
- Stay inside your listed files in scope. If the fix genuinely needs a file outside them, stop and report rather than widening.
notes: test_command_template resolves the MAIN checkout's .venv from inside any worktree (a worktree has no .venv of its own). On Windows use .venv/Scripts/python.exe.
